name: Fairchild PT-19 / PT-26 Cornell
summary: Wooden-winged Fairchild primary trainer that was USAAF's first-phase trainer for WWII, produced as inline-powered PT-19, radial-powered PT-23 and canopy-covered PT-26 Cornell.

wings: Low, cantilever wing with a wide centre section and tapered outer panels
engines: Inline-looking inverted six-cylinder (Ranger) nose on PT-19/26 or a small radial on PT-23
Thin, slightly drooped cowl with a two-blade propeller
fuselage: Two seats in tandem under open cockpits (PT-19) or a long sliding canopy (PT-26)
Fixed main gear with streamlined legs
tail: Conventional tail with a tall rounded fin

tellTales: Low-wing tandem trainer with a slim inline-engine nose and no wing bracing
Long sliding canopy over tandem seats (or open cockpits) with a rounded tail
Fixed main gear with streamlined legs and a trim fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Valiant is a heavier airplane with a big radial in a bulky cowl and a long greenhouse; the Cornell is lighter with a slim nose (or small radial) and an unbraced wing.
The Ryan has a very short, clean fuselage with wheel spats and a smaller radial or inline; the Cornell has a longer nose and wider-looking wing centre section.
The Stearman is a biplane; the Cornell is a low-wing monoplane.
The Texan has retractable gear and a big radial; the Cornell has fixed gear and a light, slim nose.
